finding.title: Add unit tests for lib/app/bootstrap/** — the entire app-startup sequence has zero automated test coverage
finding.why: A repo-wide grep for bootstrapAccount, bootstrapAnalytics, bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers, bootstrapFirebase, bootstrapNotifications, and bootstrapSeedDb returns zero hits anywhere under test/ — none of the 7 non-trivial bootstrap files (all but the 1-line logger_bootstrap.dart) are referenced by any unit, widget, or story-acceptance test. Several of these take cleanly injectable dependencies (AppLogger, a databasesPath String, a ProviderContainer) specifically designed for testability, not deep Firebase-SDK plumbing — account_bootstrap.dart in particular is the function that decides WHICH ACCOUNT'S DATABASE the whole app session opens (a multi-account, privacy-relevant decision with an error-fallback path), yet it has no regression protection at all. Any future refactor of the bootstrap sequence (a churn-prone area per the digest's own hotspot list, which includes several files immediately downstream of this one) can silently break account resolution or notification wiring with nothing in CI to catch it.
finding.recommendation: Add test/app/bootstrap/{account,notifications,seed}_bootstrap_test.dart covering success/fallback/exception branches with fakes, and a test for bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers asserting both FlutterError.onError and PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError get installed and forward to a fake AppLogger.
acceptance_criteria: account_bootstrap.dart has a test covering: account found, no account, and exception-during-resolution (asserts fallback to 'learning_tracker').
notifications_bootstrap.dart and seed_bootstrap.dart each have a test covering their success path and their catch-and-{log,rethrow} path.
bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers has a test asserting both global error hooks are installed and call the injected AppLogger.

finding.title: Close the DeviceRegistryDatabase connection on account_bootstrap.dart's exception path
finding.why: `registry.close()` sits at the end of the try block, not in a finally. If sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() (line 30) or registry.findById() (line 33) throws, execution jumps straight to the outer catch (line 51), which logs and returns a fallback filename WITHOUT ever closing the Drift-backed device_registry connection — the exact 'I/O fails halfway' scenario the Nygard lens asks about. Impact is low in practice (this runs once per app process at startup), but a leaked native database handle held for the app's whole lifetime is still an avoidable defect, and it would compound if this code path were ever retried (e.g. a future hot-reattempt) or re-used in a longer-lived context.
finding.recommendation: Move `final registry = ...` construction above a try/finally (or wrap the resolveActiveAccountId/findById calls in try{...}finally{ await registry.close(); }) so every exit path closes the connection.
acceptance_criteria: registry.close() executes on both the success path and any exception path out of bootstrapAccount.
A unit test makes sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() throw and asserts the registry/executor was still closed.

finding.title: Deduplicate 5 shadowed top-level keys in app_he.arb/app_en.arb — one silently kills a zero-task notification branch
finding.rule: Rule 0 gap (no duplicate-key checker for ARB files)
finding.why: JSON's last-key-wins behavior is confirmed against the generated Dart output: lib/l10n/app_localizations_he.dart's todaysLearning(count), errorLoadingTasks(error) and notificationReminderBody(taskCount, curriculumCount) all match the SECOND (later) ARB definition, not the first. No checker anywhere (make audit, arb-parity, flutter analyze) catches a duplicate top-level key within a single ARB file, so 3 of the 5 duplicate pairs carry genuinely different text: an editor who fixes the first (now-dead) copy of todaysLearning or errorLoadingTasks has the fix silently discarded. Worse, notificationReminderBody's line-1765 definition had a deliberately-written zero-task branch (he: 'אין משימות להיום — שמרו על הרצף!' / en: 'No tasks today — stay on track!'); a later duplicate insertion at line 2636/2834 (identical pattern in app_en.arb) replaced it with a two-way plural that has no zero case at all. It is not live-broken today only because the sole caller, lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:517, has an unrelated 'D2 fix' guard (`if (taskCount == 0) { cancel; return; }`) that happens to prevent taskCount=0 from ever reaching the l10n call — if that guard is ever removed or a second caller is added, Intl.pluralLogic falls to `other` and produces 'You have 0 tasks…' instead of the friendly copy that still sits, unused, in the file. The identical 5-key duplicate set exists in app_en.arb too, confirming this is a systemic missing-checker gap, not a one-off typo.
finding.recommendation: Add a Rule-0 checker (tool/ script or a test/l10n/ test) that fails when any top-level key string appears more than once in app_en.arb or app_he.arb, wired into make audit/ci. Then resolve the 5 duplicates: keep todaysLearning's parameterized form (matches its @todaysLearning metadata), keep errorLoadingTasks's live copy or fix the grammar deliberately, and decide whether notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch should be restored (and its caller's guard removed) or the dead ARB text deleted — don't leave orphaned content either way.
acceptance_criteria: A new checker/test fails when a top-level ARB key is duplicated, and is part of make audit or make ci.
app_en.arb and app_he.arb each contain todaysLearning, errorLoadingTasks, today, notificationReminderTitle, and notificationReminderBody exactly once.
notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch is either wired to a real caller or its vestigial ARB text is removed — no orphaned/unused ICU branch remains.

finding.title: Rewrite AN-6/AN-8 regression tests to exercise real app_shell.dart / persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart instead of hand-copied replicas
finding.rule: TQ-8 (regression test must actually guard the fix)
finding.why: Both files were written to pin fixes for shipped, user-visible bugs (AN-6: DASHBOARD nav label truncates at font_scale 1.3; AN-8: a signed-in account chip overlays the sign-in screen), but neither imports the file it claims to guard. app_shell_an6_test.dart's only imports are flutter/material.dart and flutter_test.dart — it defines and tests _ShellNavItemReplica, a hand-copied literal duplicate of the real (private) _ShellNavItem in lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:341-365; today the two happen to share the same padding/margin values, but nothing keeps them in sync. persistent_switcher_scaffold_an8_test.dart's only import is flutter_test.dart — its _authRouteNames set duplicates the literal set inside the real _isAuthSurface() at lib/app/router/persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart:92-98, and every assertion (e.g. expect(_authRouteNames.contains('SignInRoute'), isTrue)) is tautologically true by construction, since the test built the set itself. Repo-wide grep confirms no other test imports persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart for this scenario, so this is the ONLY regression coverage for AN-8, and it is vacuous: if a future edit drops 'SignInRoute' from the real _isAuthSurface() set (reintroducing AN-8), both this test and app_shell_an6_test.dart's counterpart would stay green while the bug ships again.
finding.recommendation: For AN-6, pump the real AppShell/_ShellNavItem widget tree (as test/core/navigation/app_shell_test.dart already does for other AppShell scenarios) instead of a private replica class. For AN-8, either widget-test PersistentSwitcherScaffold directly with a router stub set to each route name, or extract _isAuthSurface's route-name set into a small @visibleForTesting top-level constant the test imports, so an edit to the real set changes the test's actual input.
acceptance_criteria: app_shell_an6_test.dart imports and pumps the real _ShellNavItem/AppShell widget, not a private replica.
persistent_switcher_scaffold_an8_test.dart imports persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart, and temporarily removing 'SignInRoute' from the real _isAuthSurface() set turns the test red.

finding.title: Split device_restore_screen_l1_test.dart (810L) and app_localizations_coverage_test.dart (1482L) under the AG-3 400-line cap

evidence.quote: /// Smoke-coverage test for AppLocalizations: instantiates the concrete

finding.why: AG-3 caps hand-written Dart files at 400 lines (generated files exempt) to bound the size of any single reviewable unit; wc -l shows these two hand-written test files at 810 and 1482 lines — 2x and 3.7x over. No Rule-0 checker currently enforces this (AG-3 is [P]ending per the standards doc), so nothing flags new files as they grow past the cap.
finding.recommendation: Split device_restore_screen_l1_test.dart by RestoreStatus branch (idle/checking/restoring/complete/error/navigation) into multiple files under test/app/restore/. For app_localizations_coverage_test.dart, see the companion finding on its content — the fix there (delete or replace) also resolves this file's AG-3 violation.
acceptance_criteria: A line-count checker (tool/ script or Makefile grep) enumerates hand-written .dart files >400 lines, wired into make audit.
Neither file appears in that checker's output after the split/rewrite.
